outcome: Improvement in Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)
Complications (Acute pulmonary edema, Cardiogenic shock, Thromboembolic complications)
cohort: The study included 40 women diagnosed with Peripartum Cardiomyopathy admitted to a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Early detection and intervention with standard heart failure drugs led to better recovery rates in participants with Peripartum Cardiomyopathy, characterized by improved LV systolic function and reduced complications and deaths, which were more common in severely affected patients.
